claim_being_audited: That the model can be certified for launch because aggregate readiness passed and rollout controls are in place, provided the unresolved construction-site-safety limitation is explicitly disclosed in the model card.
decision_criteria: A compliant certification requires admissible evidence that the material limitation is either resolved, excluded from exposure, or covered by approved risk acceptance, or else that required disclosure will be made before launch.
Aggregate readiness and absence of severity-one rehearsal incidents support general readiness but do not by themselves satisfy the disclosure policy.
Rollback, monitoring, and a 7% rollout are not sufficient under the stated policy when the affected segment remains exposed.
evidence_requests: Provide the actual model-card draft or release artifact showing the construction site safety limitation is explicitly disclosed.
Provide evidence that this disclosure is a binding pre-launch requirement or approved launch condition.
Provide either approved risk acceptance that specifically addresses construction site safety exposure or evidence that the affected segment is excluded from launch.
specific_concerns: The affected construction site safety segment remains below target and is still included in the initial rollout cohort.
The policy text says rollout controls do not remove disclosure duties when the affected segment remains exposed.
The only risk-acceptance record is an incomplete draft with a blank approver line and no mention of the construction site safety exposure.
There is no admissible evidence that the required model-card disclosure has actually been prepared, reviewed, or tied as a launch condition.
unsupported_claims: The packet supports that disclosure would be the correct mitigation path, but it does not support that certification is presently compliant absent evidence the disclosure will in fact be issued before launch.
The packet does not show approved risk acceptance covering the exposed construction site safety segment.
The packet does not show that rollout controls themselves mitigate the weakness under policy, because the affected use case is not excluded.
